public_rationale: The first part holds. Oracle said on April 22, 2026 that only about 200MW was operating at Abilene, which matches his 'around 200MW'. The forecast part does not hold on a plain reading. He said more power would not be available for a year or more. Instead, Oracle said 42% of the 1.2 GW campus was delivered by June 2026. On September 10, 2026 it said six of eight buildings, 618MW, were delivered with 131,000 GPUs installed. That is about three times the 200MW within six months of the post. The report he cited from The Information may have meant power for six extra expansion buildings only, which is not yet testable.
limitations: Under the narrower reading (power for expansion buildings only), the forecast is not due until about March 2027.
'Delivered' megawatts are Oracle's measure and may not equal energized power in every case.
Key figures come through secondary sources quoting Oracle.

Part 2 (forecast): plain reading is that more power at Abilene, beyond about 200MW, would not be available for at least a year after the post, i.e., not before about March 10, 2027.

The Information's report, as summarized elsewhere, was about power for six additional expansion buildings. A reader of his sentence would take it to mean the Stargate site as a whole, so I use that plain reading and flag the difference.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Abilene had much more than 200MW in March 2026, or substantially more power came online there before March 2027.
